subject: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — leveling decision and offer next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — initial packet

Hi team,

I'm attaching the calibration packet for candidate D-129 (applied to ML Engineer). Hiring manager Anne Rhodes flagged unclear levelling between L5 and L6 because the candidate's past role had broad product ownership but the team here would still be individual-contributor focused for the first 6–12 months.

Attachments: calibration-packet-D129.pdf, jd-l5-ml-engineer.docx, scope-impact-matrix.xlsx

Key points in the packet:
- Candidate has five years of production ML systems experience; last role titled "Senior ML Engineer" at a smaller startup (scope = team of 3, cross-functional leadership for two features).
- Delivered infra/serving work and owned a model retraining pipeline; limited experience running org-level roadmap decisions.
- Hiring manager wants to offer at L6 if we treat external scope as equivalent; compensation would need benched approval (L6 base ~20% higher and changes to equity bands).

Ask: Can we align on whether this should be an L5 (strong IC, promotion path) or L6 (immediate senior/impact expectations)? Laura — will you advise on comp band flexibility and whether we can stretch to L6 on a case-by-case?

I'll set a quick sync if folks prefer to chat.

Thanks,
Lauren
---
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Talent Partner | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — initial packet

Lauren — thanks for the packet. Quick thoughts after skimming:

1) The candidate's "product ownership" seems to be within a small org; at Redwood we expect L6 to influence cross-team prioritization and roadmaps, not just lead a feature.
2) Technical breadth looks solid for L5+; the differentiator is stakeholder influence and measurable org impact.

Two clarifying questions for Anne (copied via Lauren):
- Can Anne share 1–2 concrete examples where she'd expect the hire to make decisions that directly change other teams' roadmaps in the first 6 months?
- Is there an accelerated promotion / expectations document for hires that join at L5 but are expected to operate at L6 within 12 months?

If the answers are "no" and "no", I'm leaning toward L5 (strong IC) with a clear development plan to L6. We should be explicit in the offer about promotion milestones. Marcus — given capacity and org comp, do you see risks approving an L6 as an initial hire?

Jonas
Director, Applied ML Platforms
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — initial packet

On Tue, Nov 9, 2026 at 10:05 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> If the answers are "no" and "no", I'm leaning toward L5 (strong IC) with a clear development plan to L6.

Agree with Jonas. Operationally:
- Comp: we can stretch base / equity within the L5 band if needed for competitiveness (manager approval + finance signoff). Approving an L6 base requires VP-level calibration and an exception note; that will delay the offer by ~5–7 business days while we get signoffs.
- Promotion path: we can commit to a 9–12 month promotion review with explicit success criteria (impact metrics, cross-team influence). That language can be added to the offer letter as a growth plan but should avoid guaranteed promotion phrasing.
- Market signal: Candidate title "Senior ML Engineer" at small startup is common — title inflation exists. We should focus on measurable impact rather than external titles.

Recommendation: Offer at L5 IC with a market-competitive package (top of L5 band + equity uplift) and a documented 9-month promotion plan tied to milestones in the scope-impact matrix. If Anne insists on L6 now, we should ask for a written justification of cross-org decision-making responsibilities and secure VP approval.

I'll flag finance to be ready for a comp exception if needed.

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: jd-l5-ml-engineer.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — initial packet

+1 to Laura's recommendation. Operationally we don't have the budget headroom to expand another L6 slot this quarter without reshuffling approved hires. If Anne can point to 2 product initiatives where this hire will be the final decision-maker across teams, we can re-evaluate. Otherwise L5 with promotion plan.

Marcus
VP, ML Products
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Candidate D-129: scope vs impact matrix — initial packet

Thanks all — decision: extend offer at L5 (IC) with the following guardrails included in the offer packet and hiring brief:

- Comp: top-of-band L5 base + equity uplift (talent will provide exact numbers).
- Promotion plan: 9-month calibration review with measurable milestones from the scope-impact matrix (ownership of X pipeline, 2 cross-team projects delivering Y improvements, and peer feedback threshold).
- Title: "Senior ML Engineer (L5)" with a documented pathway to Senior+ / L6 after review.

Lauren — please proceed to draft the offer and include the scope-impact-matrix.xlsx as the role's success criteria. Copy finance on comp numbers; Laura please indicate if you want finance to bump the offer for competitiveness. I'll communicate to Anne that we value the candidate's product ownership but are aligning level to expected org-wide impact.

Final note: If Anne sends a formal case for L6 with concrete examples, we'll reconvene and escalate for VP signoff — otherwise we avoid delaying the timeline.

Jonas
Director, Applied ML Platforms
